skill.name: pitchcraft
skill.description: Create persuasive briefings for kickoffs, status updates, wrap-ups, investor pitches, and solution selling. The skill uses a five-part Hook, Context, Proposal, Evidence, Ask framework and asks for audience, metrics, risks, and missing material before drafting.
skill.summary: Draft audience-aware executive briefings with a reusable persuasion framework.
skill.author: moshuying

security_audit.summary: No credential exfiltration, malicious network activity, prompt injection, or obfuscated binary payload was found. Most static findings are false positives from documentation, code fences, package metadata, JavaScript template literals, and Chinese-language Markdown. The meaningful risk is that npm postinstall and installer paths can write skill files into hidden agent configuration directories, which should require explicit user consent.

remediation.issue: NPM postinstall writes skill files into agent configuration directories.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic postinstall installation or make it opt-in with an explicit command and clear confirmation before writing files.

remediation.issue: Installer supports global and project writes under hidden agent directories.
remediation.suggestion: Print the exact destination paths, detect existing files, and require overwrite confirmation for manual installs.

remediation.issue: Manual command snippets encourage shell-based installation from documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Document a review-first install flow and tell users to inspect SKILL.md before copying it into an agent directory.

semantic_findings.title: NPM Postinstall Modifies Agent Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The package postinstall script runs scripts/install.js and writes SKILL.md into Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex skill directories. For a community package, this can change agent behavior during npm install without a separate interactive confirmation step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: package.json directly registers a postinstall command, and install.js creates/copies skill files into agent directories. The behavior is clear from code and is security-relevant even though no exfiltration is present.

content.value_statement: Teams often report activity without making the decision clear. Pitchcraft turns raw project facts into audience-aware briefings with evidence, risks, and a clear ask.
actual_capabilities: Guides briefings through Hook, Context, Proposal, Evidence, and Ask.
Provides templates for kickoff, status update, wrap-up, investor pitch, and solution selling.
Asks for audience role, concerns, goals, metrics, risks, and missing materials.
Applies writing rules for sourced metrics, risk judgment, and decision-ready asks.
Includes English and Simplified Chinese prompt and skill content.
Supports Claude Code, Codex-style prompts, Cursor rules, and general chat prompts.
limitations: It does not verify business metrics, market claims, or financial forecasts.
It needs user-provided facts, audience context, and evidence to produce accurate output.
It produces written briefing structure, not finished slide design or visual assets.
Its installer can write skill files into local agent configuration directories.

use_cases.title: Prepare a leadership status update
use_cases.description: Turn milestone progress, risks, and decisions into a concise update for directors or executives.

use_cases.title: Shape a project kickoff request
use_cases.description: Frame the opportunity, scope, resources, and risks needed to secure approval for a new initiative.

use_cases.title: Create an investor or customer pitch
use_cases.description: Convert product facts, market context, proof, and next steps into a persuasive pitch narrative.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic status update
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a status update for my project. Ask me for the audience, current progress, key metrics, risks, decisions needed, and next steps before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a project kickoff briefing
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare a project kickoff briefing using Hook, Context, Proposal, Evidence, and Ask. Identify missing information before writing the first draft.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite for an executive audience
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite my draft for senior leaders. Lead with why they should care, define every metric, state material risks early, and end with a clear decision request.

prompt_templates.title: Build a pitch from sparse inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as my briefing partner for an investor or customer pitch. Interview me for market pain, product stage, proof, moat, team, financials, and requested next step, then produce a persuasive narrative.

output_examples.input: A team lead needs a monthly update for a VP after a delayed integration.
output_examples.output: A concise status briefing that opens with the delay, explains root cause, shows recovery options, recommends one path, and asks for a dependency owner.

output_examples.input: A PM wants approval for a new analytics initiative.
output_examples.output: A kickoff narrative that connects market need to existing assets, defines scope, lists risks, and requests people, budget, and decision timing.

output_examples.input: A founder has product traction but no clear investor story.
output_examples.output: A pitch outline with a one-line value claim, market opportunity, product proof, defensibility, traction, and funding ask.

best_practices: Provide audience role, familiarity, concerns, and the decision you need.
Attach source definitions for every metric and call out uncertainty clearly.
Review the final ask before sharing so the audience has one clear next step.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to invent market data, revenue, customer quotes, or risk status.
Do not use it as a generic weekly activity log generator.
Do not hide material risks until the end of the briefing.

faq.question: What does Pitchcraft help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create structured briefings for leadership, investors, partners, and customer stakeholders.

faq.question: Does it replace my project facts?
faq.answer: No. It organizes and sharpens your facts, but you must provide accurate evidence and context.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude Code, Claude, Codex-style prompts, Cursor rules, and general AI chat prompts.

faq.question: Does it support Chinese content?
faq.answer: Yes. The repository includes Simplified Chinese README, command, skill, and prompt files.

faq.question: Can it create pitch decks?
faq.answer: It can draft the pitch narrative and structure. It does not design finished slides.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare the scenario, audience, goals, metrics, risks, evidence, and the decision or support you need.
